newsitem.title: USA: Clinton has large lead over Dole in Miami - poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton has large lead over Dole in Miami - poll.

text.p: President Clinton has a substantial lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole in the vote-rich Miami area, according to an opinion poll published Friday in the Miami Herald.
The Herald/NBC 6 poll, conducted Oct. 25-28, found that Clinton lead Dole by 61 to 34 percent among Dade County voters, with Reform Party candidate Ross Perot at 5 percent.
No Democratic presidential candidate since 1976 has come close to matching the margin that the poll suggests Clinton could get, the newspaper said.
However, the Republican had strong support among Cuban-American voters, who backed Dole by 64 to 32 percent, the poll found. His lead among all Hispanic voters in Dade County was 53 to 42 percent.
But among the county's black and non-Hispanic white voters Clinton held strong leads, with 95 percent and 65 percent support respectively, the newspaper said.
Florida's 25 electoral votes are considered a key prize in the race for the presidency and southern Florida is the state's most densely populated area.
